claims.text: RWY Theorem 4.8 gives two integral generating families for \(J_v\): the right-adjoined and lower-adjoined families. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876]

groundings.excerpt:
864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.

claims.text: RWY Conjecture 4.10 asserts that both families are minimal. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]

groundings.excerpt:
938: 4.5. A minimality conjecture
939: As we shall see in a moment,
940: our generators for I_{w} are not minimal. However,
941: we believe the following holds:
942: Conjecture 4.10 .
943: The two generating sets for the ideal J_{v_{r,s,t,n}} given in Theorem 4.8
944: are both minimal.
945: Via computer, we have verified this conjecture for all bigrassmannian permutations
946: where r\leq 4 and n-r\leq 5.

claims.text: St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), proves minimality only of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
The same paper’s Corollary 4.6 again formally concludes minimality only for the lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]

Its Remark 4.7 identifies the right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) as conjugate to the proved family and says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments; it does not state a transposed theorem or corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
